what: A single wide-tracked line of text sits faintly (.22) in the middle of a dark panel, and the same text lights up one character at a time in .3s following real progress (receiving, building). If no progress is reported, it runs over a minimum of 2.6s. Once fully lit, the text fades in .4s, and the panel rests .3s then lifts away in .9s

options.min: Minimum time until fully lit (ms), default 2600 — 0 follows progress only
options.hold: Delay from all lit to starting to walk (ms), default 50 — the original checks readiness every 50ms
options.wait: With event, the last letters are held back until fx:ready is sent to the panel (fx:progress detail 0..1 for intermediate progress). By default it finishes after the minimum time
options.--fx-dur / --fx-delay: Duration and pause of the panel lifting (CSS variables), default .9s · .3s
options.[data-fx-part=line]: Text line, containing base (faint background text) and fill (matching text that lights up)

use: Loading, please waitLoading, please wait

from.where: shared.js loader (.pk-loader) — original .preloader (panel opacity .9s ease .3s · text line .4s · background text .22 · fill .85)

note: The original follows the real progress (Pace) of the text receiving the model — to use it that way, wait: event; Set min: 0 and send fx:progress·fx:ready. When everything has lifted, the panel gets is-done and the fx:loaded event bubbles up — the original brings in the first section text 1.5s later. For screens opened often like apps, use min: 0 so it only follows progress
